title: improv·artist · patterned (Bridget Riley)
mutation_directive: improv artist: patterned via Bridget Riley

improv_extras.practice: op-art; black-and-white waves and dot-fields that pulse on the retina

v1.feedback: The piece is an L-system tree with Riley wave-bands bolted on — the comment literally says 'L-system DNA (inherited from fnx)'. Riley's op-art is fundamentally flat, precise, and retinal; draping horizontal y-snapping over a 3D branching structure with orbit controls produces a glowing particle tree, not pulsing stripe fields. A refined version should abandon the tree scaffold entirely: lay particles on a flat grid or concentric rings, apply sinusoidal displacement to rows/columns so moiré interference emerges, use hard black-and-white contrast (not additive-blended cream on dark), and lock the camera to a frontal orthographic view so the optical illusion hits the retina as Riley intended.

v2.feedback: The step(0.0, vDensity) on a sin*sin product tends toward a randomized checkerboard rather than Riley's signature flowing parallel bands with controlled local distortion. Replace the dual-frequency interference with a single dominant wave direction (e.g. just sin(gp.y * freq + displacement)) and use the twist solely for spatial warping of that band structure. Point size at 2.2px is slightly too fine for retinal shimmer — bumping to 3.0-3.5 and tightening the grid spacing would give the dense dot-field look of Riley's 'Hesitate' or 'Fragment' series where adjacency creates the optical buzz.
